A two-panel boundary correspondence materially clarifies which vertical side maps to which exterior ray, and why the bottom edge covers the intervening interval. This is warranted expository diagram scope, not an assertion that the existing proof needs a diagram.

diagram_math_checks.objects: S={-π/2<Re z<π/2, Im z>0}; H={Im w>0}; interior arrow w=sin z
diagram_math_checks.check: Local supplier thm-sine-biholomorphism-from-upper-half-strip Statement and proof steps 2.1–5.1 give sin:S→H bijective and holomorphic with holomorphic inverse. The two shaded regions and central arrow represent precisely these domain/codomain objects; no metric or linear scale correspondence is asserted.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Left boundary z=-π/2+iy and right boundary z=π/2+iy, y≥0
diagram_math_checks.check: Assigned Example identity and Verification 1.1 give images -cosh y and cosh y. From the locally defined cosh y=(exp y+exp(-y))/2, cosh(0)=1 and cosh increases unboundedly for y>0. Thus upward left-side parameter motion maps leftward along (-∞,-1], while upward right-side motion maps rightward along [1,∞). The actual arrows have these respective directions.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Bottom boundary z=x, -π/2≤x≤π/2, and corner points
diagram_math_checks.check: Assigned Example formula and Verification 2.1 identify sin x on the real axis. On this interval sin is increasing, with derivative cos x>0 in the interior and endpoint values sin(±π/2)=±1. Consequently the bottom arrow from left to right maps from -1 toward 1. Corner dots are explicitly boundary points excluded from S, as the Remarks states, rather than interior points.

Hence the displayed boundary formulas describe its continuous extension, without claiming that boundary points belong to the biholomorphism domain. Existing Facts and Verification remain byte-identical; their rigorous argument does not refer to the new figure.
